question.knowledge_point: Calculating the Second Derivative at a Point on a Solution Curve
question.problem: The function $y=f(x)$ satisfies the differential equation ${y}^{′}=\frac{1}{y}+\operatorname{ln}⁡x.$ Given that the point $(1,1)$ lies on the graph of the function, what is the value of ${{y}^{″}|}_{(1,1)}?$
question.worked_solution:
To find an expression for the second derivative, we differentiate the equation with respect to $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}({y}^{′})^{′} & ={(\frac{1}{y})}^{′}+{(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)}^{′} \\ {y}^{″} & =-\frac{1}{{y}^{2}}\cdot {y}^{′}+\frac{1}{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that we used the chain rule to compute ${(\frac{1}{y})}^{′}.$

Now, we substitute the given expression for ${y}^{′}$ into the above and simplify the resulting expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{″} & =-\frac{1}{{y}^{2}}\cdot {y}^{′}+\frac{1}{x} \\ {y}^{″} & =-\frac{1}{{y}^{2}}\cdot (\frac{1}{y}+\operatorname{ln}⁡x)+\frac{1}{x} \\ {y}^{″} & =-\frac{1}{{y}^{3}}-\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{{y}^{2}}+\frac{1}{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute the coordinates of our point into the above expression for the second derivative:

$$
\begin{aligned}{{y}^{″}|}_{(1,1)} & ={(-\frac{1}{{y}^{3}}-\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{{y}^{2}}+\frac{1}{x})|}_{(1,1)} \\  & =-\frac{1}{(1)^{3}}-\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(1)}{(1)^{2}}+\frac{1}{(1)} \\  & =-1+0+1 \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$
